name: Sydney Kamlager-Dove

statements.quote: California is the number one source of semiconductor manufacturing facilities and jobs in the country and plays a crucial role in advancing U.S. leadership in artificial intelligence. The U.S. cannot win the AI race if we do not safeguard our technological advantage, and Export Control Officers are the backbone of BIS's ability to enforce the regulations it administers.
statements.venue: Press release on committee passage of the Export Controls Enforcement Act

statements.quote: We can't just slow China down. We have to simultaneously speed up and sustain our lead in cutting edge technology,
statements.venue: Axios Pro, quoted at a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing on the BIS budget

statements.quote: a race against time, and we know that China is very proficient at replicating our advances and replicating our technology,
statements.venue: Punchbowl News, on AI chip smuggling

statements.quote: Trump rescinded the AI diffusion rule on the same day he arrived in the Middle East to announce unprecedented sales of AI chips to the UAE and Saudi Arabia before any security agreements were put in place.
statements.venue: Opening remarks at a House Foreign Affairs South and Central Asia subcommittee hearing on export controls

statements.quote: The 15% fee that Trump is planning to charge NVIDIA and AMD to sell AI chips to China is explicitly outlawed in the Export Controls Reform Act, and for good reason. It would turn export control licenses into pay-to-play arrangements that allow Trump to sideline national security considerations and extort U.S. companies.
statements.venue: Opening remarks at a House Foreign Affairs South and Central Asia subcommittee hearing on export controls

statements.quote: “It smells like it could be an illegal pay-to-play scheme,”
statements.venue: House committee hearing, quoted in the New York Post, on UAE access to AI chips

statements.quote: We have yet to have a national value-setting conversation about AI, about superintelligence. Because I think young people are getting mixed messaging. [...] It's the humans that are the guardrails and the monitors as well as the innovators.
statements.venue: Podcast interview, 'Navigating Education and Opportunity in a Changing World' (transcript)

statements.quote: We want it to augment what we do, but not replace what we do or who we are. [...] And once again, I think it goes back to us needing to have a national conversation so that Americans aren't afraid of AI, but are working together to harness it.
statements.venue: CSIS Betting on America podcast, 'Opportunity and Security in the AI Economy' (transcript)
